core_idea: For ax²+bx+c=0 (a≠0), the discriminant determines the nature of the roots.
key_formulas: Δ=b²−4ac; Δ>0: real and unequal; Δ=0: real and equal; Δ<0: non-real complex conjugates.
how_to_use: For parameter questions, form Δ and impose the required inequality or equality. For opposite-sign roots, use αβ=c/a<0.

core_idea: If α,β are roots of ax²+bx+c=0, Vieta connects the roots to the coefficients.
how_to_use: Translate statements about roots into α+β and αβ, then substitute the Vieta expressions.

core_idea: Expressions unchanged when α and β are interchanged can usually be rewritten using α+β and αβ.
how_to_use: Rewrite ratios, powers and shifted products in terms of α+β and αβ before calculating.

core_idea: Use standard algebraic identities together with the root relations from the quadratic.
how_to_use: When roots involve trigonometric or algebraic identities, combine the identity with Vieta rather than solving the roots explicitly.

core_idea: If the required roots are known, form the quadratic from their sum and product.
key_formulas: Equation with roots r₁,r₂: x²−(r₁+r₂)x+r₁r₂=0; general form ax²+bx+c=0 has sum −b/a and product c/a.
how_to_use: First find the new roots' sum and product, then construct the required equation.

core_idea: To establish the sign of a polynomial for every real x, split the real line into useful ranges and compare terms.
key_formulas: Typical ranges: x<0, 0≤x≤1, x≥1; factor or group terms so each part has a known sign.
how_to_use: Use the range that makes powers or factors comparable; avoid relying on a numerical graph for a proof.

core_idea: Powers or sequences built from quadratic roots often satisfy a recurrence inherited from the quadratic equation.
key_formulas: If α²+sα+p=0, then αⁿ=−sαⁿ⁻¹−pαⁿ⁻²; the same relation holds for β and for symmetric sums.
how_to_use: Reduce high powers using the quadratic relation instead of expanding or finding the roots explicitly.
